headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and uses MCP; firecrawl is an MCP-compatible API client that handles web content and structured data. That creates a plausible bridge where firecrawl output lands in files Continue may ingest as trusted content. No direct shared channel is documented beyond filesystem/MCP, so uncertainty stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is written into a workspace file that Continue reads automatically
IF Continue is configured to treat file contents as instructions or tool context
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of scraped files into Continue
Keep firecrawl outputs in a separate directory from active editor buffers
Add a manual review step before any MCP-fed content is passed to Continue
Use provenance tags or filenames that mark firecrawl output as untrusted
requires-engineering: enforce content provenance between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code, open editor buffers, and model-provider API keys, while firecrawl touches web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys. Both have broad network egress and can share files via the host filesystem, so sensitive workspace data could flow into firecrawl requests or outputs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default developer workflows.
conditions: IF Continue writes sensitive buffers to files that firecrawl reads or uploads
IF firecrawl is pointed at directories containing secrets or API keys
mitigations: Exclude secrets and key files from any firecrawl crawl scope
Store firecrawl artifacts outside the IDE workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after a test run
Review Continue buffer contents before invoking firecrawl on shared paths
requires-engineering: add workspace-level secret redaction before transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; firecrawl is an API client/CLI with MCP-compatible support and broad egress. Even though Continue does not modify git state, both can mutate shared files in the same workspace without documented locking, so concurrent writes or stale overwrites are plausible. The conflict is not guaranteed, but the shared filesystem makes it real.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace path concurrently
IF firecrawl CLI/API output is saved into files that Continue also edits
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repository checkout
Check file diffs before accepting either agent's changes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or instructions from workspace context, and firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data. If firecrawl output is fed into Continue without verification, Continue may propagate or act on incorrect scraped facts. Neither profile shows strong built-in verification or downstream action controls, so the cascade is plausible but not yet high severity.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is used as authoritative input to Continue
IF Continue-generated code or instructions are executed without human review
mitigations: Require human review of scraped facts before reuse
Keep firecrawl outputs as citations, not source-of-truth data
Ask Continue to cross-check key claims against a second source
Do not auto-run code generated from scraped content
requires-engineering: add verification gates between scrape and act steps

E_compliance.rationale: Continue handles source code, open editor buffers, and model-provider API keys; firecrawl handles web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a concrete mismatch cannot be proven. However, the pair can move sensitive developer data into a third-party scraping/API workflow, making compliance gaps plausible and worth treating as medium under uncertainty.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in Continue buffers or workspace files
IF firecrawl processes that regulated data through its API
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings before use
Separate API keys by environment and purpose
Log which data classes are sent to firecrawl
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
